[OBJECT] is stuck in a loop ([PERCENT] of a CPU core)

"[OBJECT]" has used [PERCENT] of one CPU core without a break for at least [MINUTES] minutes. A script that busy is almost certainly stuck in a loop: it does the same thing over and over and never stops. It slows everything else on the region down. Returning it to its owner stops it at once.
[OBJECT] has very busy scripts ([PERCENT] of a CPU core)

"[OBJECT]" has used about [PERCENT] of one CPU core over the last [MINUTES] minutes. That is far more than a normal object needs, and it slows the region down. Ask the owner to check it, or return it.
Many busy scripts add up to [CORES] CPU cores

No single object is to blame, but together the scripts here are using [CORES] CPU cores - as much as a runaway script. The busiest objects are listed below; removing or quietening a few of them will help.
[OBJECT] ([PERCENT] of a CPU core)

Physics is struggling ([PHYSFPS] fps, [ACTIVE] active objects)

The region's physics is running at [PHYSFPS] frames a second, below the warning level. That usually means objects are constantly bumping into things, spinning or tumbling, or there are too many moving physical objects ([ACTIVE] active now). The objects colliding the most are listed below. Returning them, or asking their owners to make them non-physical, will help.
